subject: Bym models - how to include variable with a std-deviation

messages.author: f9c6a2087c744460
messages.subject: Bym models - how to include variable with a std-deviation
parts:
Hi all,

I am working with inla spatial bym models of observed vs expected disease cases for large numbers of polygons.
My model specifation looks like this:

        formula1 = observed ~ 1 + f(ID, model="bym2", graph="graph.txt")

        mod1 <- inla ( formula1, data=as.data.frame(SPDF), family="poisson", E = expected,
                    control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, link=1),
                    control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE), verbose=TRUE)

So I am extending this to include a covariate (average measurement of some value per polygon) as a fixed effect like so:

       formula1 = observed ~ 1 + var1 +  f(ID, model="bym2", graph="graph.txt")

However for var1 - in addition to the measurement, I also have a standard deviation for each row of my spatial poylgons data frame.

My question is - can I include this standard deviation into the model and if so how do I specify the model ?

Many thanks,

James

messages.author: 26c971075f8aedcc
messages.subject: Re: Bym models - how to include variable with a std-deviation
parts:
James,

AFAIK the bym includes iid+spatial effect for the polygons so essentially your var1 is already included in the iid part. Given that you might consider to include the SDs as a covariate in your model, since E(x)=Var(x) when x~Poisson(). I am not sure how this plays with the observed vs. expected modelling and if SDs should be squared.

Gregor
